# Held-out native image qualification tasks

Six authored still-image tasks were frozen before their first native inference
on the vision branch at `f41e12ff3`: a new printed identifier/spatial task,
dialog screenshot, warehouse table, portrait poster, unaligned JPEG invoice,
and shape counting. They were not used to tune product kernels. No prompt
contains an expected answer. `tasks.json` fixes image hashes, geometry,
prompts and named facts/aliases. PNG/JPEG files are the runtime inputs; no font
or Pillow dependency is required by the native client.

The generator uses Pillow and an explicitly supplied DejaVu Sans font; the
manifest records their version/font hash. It refuses to overwrite frozen
tasks. Use a new directory when investigating reproduction differences:

```sh
python3 tests/fixtures/native_vision_qualification/generate.py \
  --font /path/to/DejaVuSans.ttf --output /tmp/new-heldout-fixtures
```

`reference-answers.json` contains six actual pinned Python eager target-only
answers, captured and inspected before native execution. The reference used
the same existing EXL3 checkpoint, FP16 runtime, FP8 KV, one image, no prefix
cache, an 8192-token context limit, a 4096-token prefill budget and the
4,194,304-pixel processor ceiling/minimum 65,536. It ran alone on XPU in image
`sha256:8d0e1dbe1e6a3a31e79b5ddcc1c050589c08721360af9374b9acd01236f97918`.
All eighteen named facts pass the expectations frozen beforehand. Raw learned
captures and weights are not included. The portable producer is `scripts/mm/capture_native_exl3_vision_reference.py`.
A fresh actual pinned-XPU run reproduces all six original answers and counts
exactly, with all eighteen frozen facts passing; native expectations are unchanged.
It verifies exact package/Torch-source pins and accepts caller-supplied paths.
The immutable container digest must be recorded in the external run command,
not merely passed as the declared `--runtime-image` argument.

```sh
# Run inside the already pinned custom EXL3 reference environment.
python3 scripts/mm/capture_native_exl3_vision_reference.py \
  --model MODEL_DIR \
  --runtime-image sha256:8d0e1dbe1e6a3a31e79b5ddcc1c050589c08721360af9374b9acd01236f97918 \
  --output reference-reproduction.json
```

For a CPU-only pin/fixture check add `--check-environment` and omit GPU
exposure; its result is `ENVIRONMENT_VERIFIED`, not a learned-inference pass.
The actual capture requires XPU and never substitutes CPU learned inference.
Run reference and native GPU instances sequentially. The producer performs no
service management, downloads or dependency installation; keep runtime/model
identities and external cleanup receipts alongside its output. Inspect the
reference answers before using them for any new native comparison.

Run the stdlib native client against a separately started otherwise idle
C1 image server. It submits six ordinary requests and one repeated live SSE
dialog, with temperature zero and natural EOS, and checks facts, SSE identity,
usage, repeat equality, drained gauges and proposal counters:

```sh
python3 scripts/mm/validate_native_exl3_vision_qualification.py \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model YOUR_SERVED_MODEL \
  --spec-depth 0 --output /tmp/heldout-target.json
```

Repeat on a separate native MTP3 instance with `--spec-depth 3` and a new
output path. Use page/chunk 1600, FP8 KV, prefix caching disabled and image=1.
The depth argument records the recipe; proposal counters alone do not prove
its depth. `VT_NATIVE_VISION_TRACE=2` supplies encoder and actual four-token
verification/committed-ID evidence for qualification; disable traces for
performance measurements.

The shared fact scorer accepts exact named fields and only frozen aliases;
JSON code fences and casing do not change facts. It rejects incorrect values
and never counts words elsewhere in a response as proof. Python/native JSON
formatting and token counts can differ despite equal facts; these receipts
do not certify full-tower numerics or Python/native token parity. Actual native
target-only/MTP3 runs passed all seven requests and matched 266 output IDs.
Known Merger, mixed-batch greedy and global RNG gates remain open. Broader
real-world screenshots, photographs, handwriting and OCR are not promised by
this compact suite.

## Separate resize-required screenshot

`resize-screenshot.json` freezes an 853×641 RGB derivative of the authored
backup dialog, generated by bicubic enlargement before its first inference.
It must be processed at864×640 (grid1×40×54;540 visual rows). Its original
three facts and prompt are unchanged. This is **not a seventh held-out task**;
the six-task default, original hashes and reference answers remain unchanged.
`generate_resize_screenshot.py --output NEW_DIRECTORY` reproduces the derived
PNG/manifest and refuses to overwrite either artifact.

The actual pinned Python worker passes all three facts and observes one FP16
XPU tower input with2160×1536 pixels and grid[1,40,54]. Its compact answer is
`resize-screenshot-reference.json`; raw IDs/readbacks stay local. Capture that
case with the same reference command above plus `--resize-screenshot` and a
new output path. Expose `scripts/mm` on the reference worker's `PYTHONPATH` so
its optional observation extension can be imported. The observation is only
enabled for this explicit case; no native runtime imports this code.

Run the native client on fresh, sequential C1 target-only and MTP3 instances:

```sh
python3 scripts/mm/validate_native_exl3_vision_qualification.py \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model YOUR_SERVED_MODEL \
  --spec-depth 0 --resize-screenshot --output target-resize.json
# On a separate MTP3 instance, use depth3 and a new output file.
```

This submits one ordinary and one SSE request. Both actual modes pass all
facts, natural EOS, repeat/stream equality and597/36/633 usage. Each encodes
the derivative once with540 rows; MTP3 proposes54 tokens. The independent
checker confirms72 exact committed output IDs per mode (two36-token answers),
including scheduler EOS trimming. Python uses31 output tokens and different
JSON formatting; equal facts do not imply Python/native token equality.

```sh
python3 -O scripts/mm/check_native_exl3_vision_resize_screenshot.py \
  --reference reference-resize.json --reference-execution reference-exit.json \
  --target target-resize.json --target-trace target-server.log \
  --target-execution target-exit.json \
  --mtp mtp-resize.json --mtp-trace mtp-server.log --mtp-execution mtp-exit.json \
  --generation-config MODEL_DIR/generation_config.json --output resize-check.json
```

Keep supervised exit receipts alongside the captures. Reference receipts bind
actual immutable image identity, exit0, result SHA-256, removed instance and
stopped production. Native receipts additionally bind client exit0, result and
trace hashes, manifest/reference hashes in `sources`, native binary/head and
declared depth. The checker requires progressing actual C1 graph shapes1/4,
one encode per instance, drained request gauges and exact committed IDs; it
does not accept a successful client status alone. Three optimized-Python
negatives reject missing cleanup, fabricated encoder rows and changed sampled
IDs at the intended guards. The numbers above are historical, fixture-specific
observations. Use the generators and checker above with new supervised receipts
to evaluate another source/binary head; the development run capsule is not a
runtime input or final-head qualification. Full-tower numerics, mixed-batch
greedy invariance and PR-head readiness remain open.
